title: Best Indian catering companies in Dubai 2026
body_markdown:
The best fit for an Indian catering Dubai enquiry is the company whose proposal matches your menu, dietary requirements, venue and service format—not simply the longest dish list. Compare a staffed buffet, a plated dinner and food delivery against the same brief. Then check who handles setup, replenishment, clearing and equipment before you choose.


**TL;DR**

- For Indian catering Dubai enquiries, compare menu detail, staffing, dietary handling and venue requirements before choosing.
- myCHEF provides private chefs and event catering; request an Indian menu proposal for your specific occasion.
- A staffed buffet suits flexible dining; plated service suits a seated programme; drop-off requires a host-side plan.
- Choose the clearest complete proposal, not the longest menu or an unexplained headline quotation.


## What makes an Indian catering proposal worth shortlisting?

**Choose the proposal that explains how your guests will eat, not just what they will eat.** A menu can look right while leaving important responsibilities unresolved: who brings serving dishes, who replenishes the buffet and who clears the kitchen afterwards.

myCHEF provides private chefs and event catering for households and businesses in Dubai. Use the [event catering enquiry page](https://www.mychef.ae/contact) to request a proposal for your occasion, including your preferred Indian dishes and service requirements. Ask for written confirmation of the menu and arrangements rather than assuming a particular package is included.

Judge every proposal against these criteria:

- **Menu fit:** named dishes, regional preferences, spice levels and suitable accompaniments.
- **Dietary clarity:** specific ingredients, exclusions and preparation arrangements.
- **Service ownership:** clear responsibility for setup, serving, replenishment and clearing.
- **Venue fit:** a workable plan for access, kitchen use and equipment.
- **Complete scope:** inclusions, exclusions and changes recorded in writing.

A useful shortlist does not need an unsupported company leaderboard. It needs comparable answers to the questions that determine whether your event will run as intended.

## Which Indian catering format fits your event?

Start with the service format before comparing companies. A delivery proposal and a fully staffed dinner are different services, even when their menus contain similar dishes.

The options below are planning choices, not advertised myCHEF packages. Confirm which arrangements a caterer can provide for your date and venue.

| Format | Best for | Main advantage | Key limitation | Confirm before choosing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Staffed Indian buffet | Celebrations where guests want choice | Guests choose dishes and portions | Needs serving space and a replenishment plan | Buffet equipment, service staff and clearing |
| Plated Indian dinner | Seated occasions with a defined programme | Courses follow an agreed sequence | Requires coordinated kitchen and table service | Dietary alternatives, service timing and workspace |
| Indian sharing menu | Home dinners centred on the table | Guests pass dishes without leaving their seats | Serving bowls compete with place settings | Table capacity and replacement of shared dishes |
| Drop-off Indian catering | Informal gatherings with a host-side team | Separates food provision from event staffing | Serving and cleanup need separate ownership | Delivery handover, equipment and food instructions |

### Staffed Indian buffet: best for guest choice

A buffet lets guests select from the agreed menu rather than receive the same plated meal. It suits celebrations where people want different combinations of rice, breads, curries and sides.

**Buffet advantages:**

- Guests choose their preferred dishes.
- Dietary options can have clearly identified serving positions.
- The menu can include contrasting flavours and textures.

**Buffet limitations:**

- The venue needs space for the serving area and guest movement.
- Replenishment and serving utensils need active management.

**Verdict: Choose a staffed buffet when choice matters and the venue can accommodate it.**

### Plated Indian dinner: best for a structured evening

A plated dinner brings each course to seated guests. This format suits an occasion built around speeches, presentations or a shared dining sequence.

**Plated dinner advantages:**

- Guests remain seated during service.
- Each dietary alternative can be assigned to a named guest.
- The meal has a clear beginning, progression and finish.

**Plated dinner limitations:**

- The caterer needs suitable preparation and plating space.
- Late arrivals and programme changes need a service plan.

**Verdict: Choose plated service when the meal should follow the event programme.**

### Indian sharing menu: best for a conversational home dinner

A sharing menu places dishes on the dining table for guests to pass. It creates a different experience from a buffet because guests stay together rather than leave their seats to serve themselves.

**Sharing menu advantages:**

- Guests can try different dishes while remaining seated.
- The table becomes the centre of the meal.
- Hosts can plan the food around a familiar family-style format.

**Sharing menu limitations:**

- Serving bowls reduce space for glasses, plates and decorations.
- Shared utensils need careful management when dietary restrictions differ.

**Verdict: Choose sharing dishes when the table has enough room for both guests and food.**

### Drop-off Indian catering: best for host-managed gatherings

Drop-off catering supplies the agreed food without assuming a complete event service. Your brief must establish what happens after delivery, particularly if you do not have staff at the venue.

**Drop-off advantages:**

- The food handover can be planned separately from guest arrivals.
- You retain control over the dining timetable.
- It suits a gathering where someone already owns setup and serving.

**Drop-off limitations:**

- Delivery does not establish who serves or clears.
- Equipment, presentation and handling instructions require confirmation.

**Verdict: Choose drop-off only when someone is responsible for the meal after handover.**

## How should you brief an Indian caterer?

Send every shortlisted company the same brief. Otherwise, you risk comparing a proposal that includes event staff with another that covers food alone.

Begin with the occasion, date, Dubai location and guest count. Separate adults and children where their menus or portions need to differ, and explain whether guests will eat together or arrive throughout the event.

Then describe the food in concrete terms. “Indian menu” leaves too much open; named dishes and regional preferences give the caterer something useful to respond to.

Include:

- Dishes you definitely want and ingredients you want excluded.
- Vegetarian, vegan and other dietary requirements.
- Preferred spice levels, including a separate children's option if needed.
- Buffet, plated, sharing or delivery-only service.
- Guest arrival, meal service and event finish times.
- Kitchen facilities, access restrictions and available dining space.

**For a private dinner or catered celebration, myCHEF is relevant when you want to discuss both the chef service and the event requirements.** Request confirmation that the proposed Indian menu, staffing and equipment match your brief.

Do not treat a dish name as a complete specification. Ask about the preparation, accompaniments and serving style when those details matter to your guests.

## What should a balanced Indian event menu include?

Build the menu around how guests will eat, rather than adding dishes until the list looks generous. Check that vegetarian guests have a complete meal, that accompaniments suit the mains and that the service plan accounts for dishes intended to arrive freshly prepared.

The following is an **illustrative menu brief**, not a myCHEF menu or package:

- **Arrival food:** a small savoury bite, with a clearly identified vegetarian alternative.
- **Main dishes:** a vegetable-led dish, a lentil dish and a meat or fish dish if requested.
- **Accompaniments:** rice, an agreed bread selection and suitable chutneys or sides.
- **Dessert:** an Indian sweet or another agreed finish suited to the event.

Ask the caterer to suggest a coherent selection rather than automatically including every category. A vegetarian celebration needs a different brief from a mixed menu, and a standing reception needs food that works without a full place setting.

If you want regional specificity, name it. Discuss the dishes you mean instead of asking the caterer to interpret a broad label such as “traditional Indian”.

## How do buffet and plated proposals differ?

**Compare the same menu and guest count before judging the service-format difference.** A buffet proposal and a plated proposal can include different dishes, equipment and staffing, so the total alone does not explain the difference.

Ask each company to separate food, service staff, equipment and venue-related requirements in its proposal. Then check whether delivery, setup, clearing and collection are included or handled separately.

For a wedding or formal celebration, a [buffet versus plated dinner cost comparison](https://blog.gabbeys.com/wedding-catering-cost-buffet-vs-plated-dinner) starts with matching the scope: a self-service buffet and a staffed plated dinner assign different responsibilities to the catering team.

The main decision is not whether one format is universally better. It is whether the service arrangement supports your event.

- Choose a buffet when guest choice and flexible portions are priorities.
- Choose plated service when the programme depends on coordinated courses.
- Ask for both options only if the venue can realistically support either.

Before accepting, check the assumptions behind each proposal. A change in guest count, menu, equipment or service duration needs a clear approval process.

## Which dietary questions need written answers?

Describe dietary requirements precisely. Vegetarian, vegan, halal and allergy-related requests are not interchangeable, and the menu should identify what each affected guest can eat.

Some Indian dishes use dairy, nuts or wheat. Ask about ingredients dish by dish rather than assuming that a familiar name tells you everything about its preparation.

For allergies, explain the specific allergen and ask the caterer what preparation and service arrangements they can provide. Do not interpret an ingredient omission as confirmation of separate preparation or separate utensils.

Useful questions include:

- Which dishes meet each guest's stated requirements?
- Which ingredients appear in sauces, garnishes and accompaniments?
- How will dishes and dietary alternatives be identified during service?
- Who answers ingredient questions at the event?
- What arrangements can the kitchen support for an allergy request?

**Keep allergy requirements separate from taste preferences in your brief.** Both deserve attention, but they require different conversations and clear written responses.

## What must the venue be ready for?

A suitable menu still needs a workable venue plan. Ask the caterer what they need before agreeing where the buffet, plating area or service station will go.

Confirm these practical arrangements:

- **Access:** the delivery entrance, parking arrangements and route to the kitchen.
- **Kitchen:** the equipment and preparation space available for agreed use.
- **Service space:** room for the buffet, plating or shared dishes.
- **Clearance:** where used crockery, equipment and waste will go.


![Four venue checks covering access, kitchen, service space and clearance](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/afa8b692-6952-4608-8933-8b5baf6bc447/body-39470650de87545406adb498bd485804.jpg)

*Agree the working areas before finalising the catering setup.*


For an apartment, check building access and lift arrangements with the venue contact. For a villa, explain whether cooking and dining will happen indoors, outdoors or across separate areas.

For an office, identify who approves kitchen use and who receives the catering team. Do not assume that reception, security or facilities staff already have the event details.

## Who handles serving and cleanup?

Write down responsibilities before confirming the event. “Catering included” does not answer whether someone lays the table, replenishes dishes, clears plates or removes hired equipment.

Ask for a named point of contact and a clear division between the catering team, venue team and host. If responsibilities overlap, resolve them before event day rather than leaving staff to negotiate during service.

Use a simple checklist:

- Who sets up food and dining equipment?
- Who serves and replenishes dishes?
- Who clears tables and the working kitchen area?
- Who collects equipment, and when?
- Who approves changes during the event?

Specify what “cleanup” means for your venue. Clearing food-service equipment and cleaning the entire event space are different tasks.

## FAQ


**What's the best way to compare Indian catering companies in Dubai?**

Compare written proposals against the same menu, guest count, venue and service brief. Check staffing, equipment, dietary arrangements and clearing responsibilities before choosing.

**Is a buffet better than a plated Indian dinner?**

A buffet is better for guest choice, while plated service suits a structured seated programme. Choose according to your event and venue rather than treating either format as universally better.

**Can I ask myCHEF for an Indian catering proposal?**

You can send myCHEF an enquiry describing your preferred Indian menu and event requirements. Request confirmation of the dishes, chef service, staffing and equipment that can be included.

**What should I include in an Indian catering enquiry?**

Include the date, location, guest count and service required. Add preferred dishes, dietary requirements, meal timing and details of the kitchen or venue facilities.

**Does drop-off catering include serving staff?**

Do not assume drop-off catering includes serving staff. Ask the company to confirm who handles setup, serving, replenishment and clearing after delivery.

**Can an Indian catering menu accommodate vegetarian guests?**

Request a complete vegetarian menu or clearly identified vegetarian choices. Confirm ingredients in sauces, garnishes and accompaniments rather than relying on dish names alone.

**How do I compare catering quotations fairly?**

Compare quotations with matching menus, guest counts and service responsibilities. Ask each company to identify food, staffing, equipment and venue-related requirements so differences are clear.

- [Groceries and equipment for a private chef](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/do-private-chefs-in-dubai-bring-their-own-groceries-and-equipment)

## Send a brief that produces a useful proposal

The most revealing part of a catering proposal is often what happens around the food: access, serving, replenishment and clearing. Resolve those details alongside the menu, not after accepting it.

Send myCHEF your **date, location, guest count and service required**, together with your preferred Indian dishes and dietary requirements. Ask for a proposal that states what is included and what you or the venue need to arrange.
